target_customer: Member-based organizations (clubs, running groups, fraternal orders) paying a monthly fee for a self-branded mobile app
problem: Groups struggle to keep members informed and engaged using email, Facebook and Meetup. A dedicated app with push notifications was meant to raise involvement and event attendance.
business_model: B2B SaaS monthly subscription tiered by group size ($49, $89 and $149 per month in early 2015)
product_category: White-label mobile apps for groups and communities

founders.name: Brian Glick
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Facebook, YouTube and Google. TechCrunch 2015-02-04 says he was involved in launching Google+ Communities. Education not found.

founders.name: Julian Frumar
previous_startups: Earlier YC startup that exited to Google (name not given on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a two-time YC technical founder with one exit to Google, specializing in frontend. Education not found.

competitors.name: Facebook Groups app
competitors.what: Standalone mobile app for Facebook Groups launched as a way for groups to communicate

competitors.name: Meetup
competitors.what: Online platform for groups to organize events and members; TechCrunch named it as the incumbent way groups connect and suggested a freemium GroupAhead would compete with it

technical_complexity.rationale: A templated white-label iOS and Android app configured per group from a web dashboard with CSV member import and calendar sync. Standard mobile engineering for a two person team, with publishing per group to app stores the operational burden.

defensibility.rationale: Features were member list, calendar, discussions and announcements. Facebook Groups and other group tools offered close substitutes, and per-group app store publishing was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook released its Groups app in November 2014, shortly before the batch. No source found on any acquisition or copying of GroupAhead itself.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-02-04) reported about 16 pilot apps live on the App Store and Google Play from mid-2014 for groups such as the Freemasons and SF FrontRunners, suggesting demand from small organizations, but no revenue figures were found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. Apps were branded with each group's own logo, so the GroupAhead name was largely invisible to end users.

outcome_analysis: GroupAhead raised just under half a million dollars before YC and had a few dozen small group customers by early 2015, then became inactive. No shutdown announcement, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause of failure is not public. The product competed with free tools from Facebook and Meetup, and pricing of $49 to $149 per month to small volunteer groups suggests a small market, but that is an inference, not a sourced reason.
